shell.note: A platform admin reads no org's data. Reaching into one is a time-bounded break-glass session, and it appears in that org's own audit log.

orgs.title: Orgs
orgs.intro: Create orgs, suspend them and set their first admin. No session, member or piece of content appears here — the figures are aggregates only.
orgs.empty: No orgs yet. Start by creating one.
orgs.count: {count, plural, =0 {No orgs} one {One org} other {{value} orgs}}
orgs.suspendHint: Suspension blocks sign-in and stops scheduled jobs. It deletes nothing and it is reversible.
orgs.suspendReasonHint: The org's admins read it in their own audit log.
orgs.deleteHint: Deletion removes the org's rows and its files together and cannot be undone. If the intent is to stop access for now, suspension is what you want.
orgs.deleteSlugIntro: To confirm, type the org's slug exactly as shown:
orgs.deleteQueued: Deletion has started. The org is suspended now; its rows and files are removed in the background.

newOrg.title: New org
newOrg.intro: There is no org self-registration. A platform admin creates one, and the creation is written to that org's audit log.
newOrg.errorSummaryTitle: The org could not be created
newOrg.nameHint: In Arabic, as members will see it.
newOrg.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It never changes after creation.
newOrg.prefixHint: Two to five Latin letters, shown in capitals in every certificate number.
newOrg.domainsHint: One domain per line, in any case — stored in lowercase. The first sign-in from an address on one of them creates a membership.
newOrg.firstAdminHint: Becomes an org admin on their first sign-in. Changeable later.
newOrg.seedHint: Technical, administrative, creative, a lesson from experience.

domains.title: Domains and first admin
domains.domainsIntro: These decide who can be provisioned into the org on a first sign-in.
domains.removalNote: Removing a domain prevents new memberships only. Existing members keep their access.
domains.domainHint: For example example.com — in any case; it is stored in lowercase, as the list shows it.
domains.removeConfirmBody: Nobody can create a new membership with an address on this domain any more. Existing members stay as they are, and nobody loses access.
domains.empty: No domains. Nobody can be provisioned into this org right now.
domains.domainCount: {count, plural, =0 {No domains} one {One domain} other {{value} domains}}
domains.firstAdminIntro: If that address is already a member they become an admin at once; if not, on their first sign-in.
domains.firstAdminHint: In any case — stored in lowercase.
domains.firstAdminSaved: The first admin's email is saved.

templates.title: Platform template library
templates.intro: This library is managed, not authored here. A platform admin has no org and the designer's editor is org-scoped, so authoring stays in an org's editor. What happens here: list, promote a published org version, set the default, retire.
templates.baselineNote: The baseline ships with the platform and is ready for every org from the moment it is created, before it publishes anything: five poster families, and three certificate families in landscape and portrait.
templates.schemesNote: Every template renders light and dark; the scheme is chosen where it is used, not in the library.
templates.floorNote: The library never falls below one default per purpose, so the last default of a purpose offers no retirement.
templates.versions: {count, plural, =0 {No versions} one {One version} other {{value} versions}}
templates.retireConfirmBody: The automatic poster and certificate paths will no longer choose it, and orgs will see it as retired. What was already exported with it stays as it is, and it can return to service.
templates.promoteIntro: Promotion is a copy. An org's later edits never reach the promoted version, which is what makes improving a platform template safe.
templates.promoteNote: Only published versions appear here, by name, family and number. No template's content is shown on this page.
templates.promoteEmpty: No published version is available to promote.
templates.promoteNameHint: Leave it empty to keep the org's name for it.
templates.promoted: The template was promoted into the library.

metrics.title: Platform metrics
metrics.intro: Aggregates only. No member name, session title or content appears here, and that is a constraint in the query rather than in the rendering.
metrics.alertsIntro: The same thresholds the worker measures every minute, as it reads them — no copy of them lives on this page.
metrics.jobsIntro: Oldest pending job is the number that catches a stalled queue; the others look healthy even when it is not.

impersonate.title: Break-glass
impersonate.honest: You cannot look at an org's data without the org knowing. The session is written to that org's own audit log the moment it starts, and its admins can see it.
impersonate.tokenTail: If the session expires on its own, access to the org can last up to 15 minutes beyond it, because the grant travels on the sign-in token until it refreshes. Ending it yourself drops it from this browser at once.
impersonate.intro: Pick the org, write the reason, set the duration. Four hours is the ceiling, and it is a database constraint rather than a rule on this page.
impersonate.reasonHint: Stored verbatim in the org's log. Write it for whoever reads it there.
impersonate.durationMinutes: {count, plural, =0 {under a minute} one {one minute} other {{value} minutes}}
impersonate.durationHours: {count, plural, =0 {under an hour} one {one hour} other {{value} hours}}
impersonate.durationCeiling: The ceiling — a database constraint, not a page setting.
impersonate.activeNote: You are inside a break-glass session.
impersonate.expiredRecently: Your session with <bdi>{org}</bdi> expired on its own at <bdi>{time}</bdi>.

banner.viewingAs: You are browsing <bdi>{org}</bdi> with break-glass access, and this session is recorded in that org's audit log.
banner.readOnly: Read-only: no privileged action inside the org can be performed.
banner.stopped: The session has ended, and the org is out of your access.
